title: Writing: style and format
subtitle: jot down, draft, write up, italics, block capitals
summary: Name every stage and every detail of writing - from scribbling and doodling to drafting, writing up, formatting, indenting and using the right kind of brackets.

lesson.heading: Writing quickly and informally
lesson.text: If you are in a hurry you **scribble** a note - you write it quickly, without much care. To **jot down** (informal) or **make a note of** (more formal) something is to write it down so that you remember it. **Doodling** is drawing and writing irrelevant things on the paper in front of you.

examples.text: I'll just **scribble** a note for Preeti to tell her where we've gone.
I'll just **jot down** your phone number before I forget it.
She got so bored at the meeting she spent the whole time **doodling**.
A note is likely to be in a more **chatty** style than, say, a business letter.
examples.note: chatty = informal, when used about writing

lesson.heading: Stages of a piece of writing
rows: make a first attempt at writing something
I'm just drafting an application letter. / the first draft of an essay
copy in writing what is spoken
Some students write down everything the lecturer says.
I'll copy out the information on hotels for you.
make a proper final written text based on previous drafts
She's writing up her dissertation at the moment, so she's very tired and stressed.
the original version produced by the author
She bought the manuscript of a famous poem at the sale.
an author's text that has not yet been published
I'll email the typescript to the publisher tomorrow.

lesson.heading: Typing and printing
lesson.text: To **touch-type** is to type using all your fingers without looking at the keyboard. To **run off** a copy is to print it out, and to **format** a text is to create the page as it will appear when printed. When you **cut and paste** or **copy and paste**, you move text from one place to another electronically.

examples.text: Learning to **touch-type** was one of the most useful things I've ever done.
Please **run off** a copy of the agenda for everyone coming to the meeting.
I've done the text, but I want to **format** it properly before printing it.
His essay was a **cut-and-paste** job straight from the internet.

lesson.note: The letters and numbers on a keyboard can all be called characters - a password often needs to be at least eight characters.

lesson.heading: Ways of marking text
columns: What it looks like or does
rows: the words sit inside a grey box
the same typeface, but bigger or smaller letters
a different design of letters altogether
double inverted commas / double quotation marks
"This sentence is in double quotation marks."
a line that begins away from the normal margin
the * symbol, often used to signal a footnote
the small dot in front of an item in a list
a number or letter written above the normal line

lesson.heading: Types of brackets and letters
rows: so i wrote to mr smith

lesson.heading: The parts of a book
lesson.text: The first page of an academic book shows the **title** (*Psychology Today*), the **subtitle** (*An introduction*), the **contents**, then **chapter headings** (*Chapter 1 What is psychology?*) and **sub-headings** within a chapter (*1.1 Some definitions*).

examples.text: My PhD thesis was called *Socialisation through children's literature* and its **subtitle** was *The Soviet example*.
Each **chapter heading** is followed by two or three **sub-headings**.

lesson.text: You draft a text first and write it up last - drafting is the rough beginning, writing up the polished end.

exercises.prompt: Let me just ___ your email address, or I'll forget it.
exercises.explanation: To jot something down is to write it down quickly so you remember it.

exercises.prompt: I'll just ___ a note for Preeti to tell her where we've gone.
exercises.explanation: To scribble is to write quickly and carelessly.

exercises.prompt: I spent the whole lesson just ___ in the margin of my exercise book, I was so bored.
exercises.explanation: Doodling is drawing and writing irrelevant things on the paper in front of you.

exercises.prompt: She's been ___ her PhD thesis for the last three months, that's why no one has seen her.
exercises.explanation: To write up a piece of work is to make the proper final text based on earlier drafts.

exercises.prompt: I'll email you a ___ of the letter, so you can suggest any changes before we send it.
exercises.explanation: A draft is a first attempt at a piece of writing.

exercises.prompt: In a bibliography, it is normal practice to put book titles in ___ rather than inverted commas.
exercises.explanation: Text can be in italics, or be described as italicised.

exercises.prompt: Your computer password should consist of at least eight ___ , with at least one number.
exercises.hint: (c...; letters and numbers on a keyboard)
exercises.explanation: The letters and numbers on a keyboard are all called characters.

exercises.prompt: Please ___ a copy of the agenda for everyone coming to the meeting.
exercises.explanation: To run off a copy is to print it out.

exercises.prompt: Writers sometimes use an ___ to indicate that there is a footnote.
Match the two halves to make compound nouns about writing and format.
Match each bracket symbol with its name.
How would you describe the way **I love the summer** is printed here?
exercises.explanation: Text printed in heavy black letters is in bold.

exercises.prompt: How would you describe WILL YOU BE QUIET!?
exercises.explanation: Capitals are also called upper case, the more technical term.

exercises.prompt: How would you describe 'so i wrote to mr smith'?
exercises.explanation: Small letters are also called lower case.

exercises.prompt: It's better to be more formal when you write an academic essay and not use such a ___ style.
exercises.explanation: A chatty style is an informal one, fine for a note but not for an essay.

exercises.prompt: I think you should ___ your CV differently if you want it to look good when it's printed out.
exercises.explanation: To format a document is to create the page as it will appear when printed.

exercises.prompt: She works in the museum, conserving ancient ___ .
exercises.hint: (plural: original versions produced by the author)
exercises.explanation: A manuscript is the original version of a text produced by its author.

exercises.prompt: You waste so much time typing with just two fingers - you really should learn to ___ .
exercises.explanation: To touch-type is to type using all your fingers without looking at the keyboard.

exercises.prompt: Mrs Ward taught the children to ___ the first line of each paragraph when they wrote stories.
exercises.explanation: An indented line begins away from the normal margin.

exercises.statement: A typescript is an author's text that has not yet been published.
exercises.explanation: Correct - you email the typescript to the publisher; a manuscript is the original version produced by the author.
